keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Erridupizir 'reigned c. 2220 – c. 2211 BC (MC)' as 'King of the Four Corners' and dedicated a statue to Enlil at Nippur; 'the Gutians are now known to have been in the area for at least a century by then'. The homeland Gutium is 'not known', so only the Mesopotamian foothold is drawn; it overlaps Akkad's -2250 shape, which the Akkad dossier leaves soft.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, bridged: the Kutik-Inshushinak page (headed Puzur-Inshushinak) does not date the conquest of Akkad but says it 'probably encroached considerably on Gutian territory, gravely weakening them, and making them unable to withstand the Neo-Sumerian revolt of Utu-hengal' (c. 2119). Placed at -2125, between his accession as crown prince (c. 2130) and the revolt. Confidence 1.

correction.text: the Third Dynasty of Ur: Sumer, Akkad and Susiana, 131,488 km2, 'from Urbilum to Pashime and Susa'; the Gutian dynasty ended c. 2119, 'marked by the accession of Uruk ruler Utu-hengal (c. 2119 - 2112 BC)'; use this outline for third-dynasty-of-ur -2112..-2004 and draw no Gutians after -2119

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's only Gutian shape is dated -2100..-2001, a century after the dynasty's end; its area and bbox (44.2–51.1 E, 30.2–33.4 N) are Ur III's realm with Susa. Reviewed again in third-dynasty-of-ur, which uses it. The short chronology (Tirigan c. 2055–2050) may explain the mislabel, but even then Ur III follows at once.

ledger.note: 2220 BCE: Erridupizir, king of Gutium, holds Adab. 'By the end of the Akkadian period, the Sumerian city of Adab was occupied by the Gutians, who made it their capital'; Erridupizir 'reigned c. 2220 – c. 2211 BC (MC)' and dedicated a statue to Enlil at Nippur. The Sumerian King List: 'In the land of Gutium, at first no king was famous; they ruled themselves for 5 years', then 21 kings 'ruled for 125 years and 40 days'. Infobox 'Established: c. 2220 BC'.

region.text: the Sumerian plain, Uruk included: Adab, Umma, Nippur, Uruk and the Tigris bank

ledger.note: 2189 BCE: the Gutians take the Sumerian plain as Akkad shrinks. Dudu (2189–2168) 'held a reduced kingdom, likely limited to northern Babylonia around Akkad and Kish'; Gutian governors at Umma ('Namahni, a governor from the time of Iarlagan of Gutium', Umma page). The year is Dudu's accession; the frontier is bridged. [fixer me-01: region aligned with akkadian-empire's loss (Sumer apart from Lagash); Uruk is lost to its own dynasty in -2154 (/ledger)]
2154 BCE: the Akkadian dynasty ends and Akkad passes to the Gutians. 'Disestablished: c. 2154 BC' (Shu-turul 2168–2154); the Gutian page's table: 'Gutian period (c. 2154 – c. 2119 BC)'.
2154 BCE: Uruk's fourth dynasty begins. 'Ur-nigin: r. c. 2154 – c. 2147 BC'; the Gutian page: 'Early Dynastic city-states such as Lagash and Uruk began to re-assert themselves'.

region.text: Akkad and Kish: 'numerous cities in central Mesopotamia, including Eshnunna and Akkad, and probably Akshak'

ledger.note: 2125 BCE (bridged): Elam takes Akkad. The page is silent on the year: 'He conquered numerous cities in central Mesopotamia, including Eshnunna and Akkad, and probably Akshak'; 'His conquests probably encroached considerably on Gutian territory, gravely weakening them, and making them unable to withstand the Neo-Sumerian revolt of Utu-hengal'. Placed shortly before the Gutian fall (c. 2119). Mirror of elam /ledger (gain of Akkad, -2125).

region.text: Sumer and 'both banks of the Tigris' to Utu-hengal (Lagash and Uruk already independent); Akkad and Kish had gone to Elam in -2125

ledger.note: 2119 BCE: Utu-hengal of Uruk defeats Tirigan. 'The end of the Gutian dynasty is marked by the accession of Uruk ruler Utu-hengal (c. 2119 - 2112 BC)'; Tirigan 'fl. c. 2120 – c. 2119 BC (MC)', 'Defeated by the Uruk king (Utu-hengal) according to victory stele erected in Uruk', captured in Dabrum after he 'had seized both banks of the Tigris River'. The short chronology puts this c. 2055–2050; 'Disestablished: c. 2119 BC'. [fixer me-01: the dissolve region is the Sumerian plain only, as uruk /ledger/1 gains it; Akkad is no longer handed to Uruk (the first version listed it): the Gutian loss of Akkad to Elam is booked at -2125.]

wars.name: Utu-hengal's war against Tirigan

zones.text: 'Both banks of the Tigris he had seized'; Dabrum, where Tirigan was taken

wars.outcome: Tirigan captured, 'the kingship of the land of Sumer' passed to Uruk; Ur-Nammu of Ur followed within seven years.
wars.note: The Gutian page names Dabrum, Karkar, Nagsu and Ili-tappe from Utu-hengal's inscription; his own page gives no battle date, only the reign c. 2119–2112.

certainty.note: Nothing is surveyed: the Gutian homeland is unknown, the Mesopotamian holdings are known from a capital (Adab), governors (Umma) and a river ('both banks of the Tigris'); every edge is bridged.

notes:
Cliopatria's single 'Gutian Dynasty' shape (-2100..-2001, 131,488 km2 over Sumer, Akkad and Susiana) is not Gutian: it is the Third Dynasty of Ur's realm, a century after the Gutians fell. It is marked wrong here and reused, with the years -2112..-2004, by the new dossier third-dynasty-of-ur. The Gutian state is redrawn from the pages as four new keyframes: Adab alone (-2220..-2190), the Sumerian plain without Lagash (-2189..-2155; Uruk is included until its dynasty begins in -2154), Akkad plus the plain without Lagash and Uruk (-2154..-2126), and the plain alone (-2125..-2119, after Elam's conquest of Akkad). Every edge is bridged (confidence 1-2): the page gives the capital, governors at Umma and 'both banks of the Tigris', never a frontier, and says of the homeland 'even their homeland is not known'.

Start year: the infobox's c. 2220 (Erridupizir, MC) is used; the page's table also offers 'Gutian period (c. 2154 – c. 2119 BC)'. The found region (Adab) overlaps the Akkadian -2250 shape for -2220..-2190; the Akkad dossier records the loss of the Sumerian plain only in 2189, so the Adab enclave double-claimed for thirty years; the me-01 fix settles it by booking the loss of Adab on the Akkad side (-2220, mirror of this found event). Alternatives: start at -2189 or -2154.

Short chronology: the page dates Erridupizir c. 2147–2138 and Tirigan c. 2055–2050 SC; the History of Sumer page gives the Gutian dynasty c. 2055–2048 SC. Not used.

Successor: the Sumerian plain to uruk (new dossier, Utu-hengal); Akkad had gone to Elam in -2125 (Puzur-Inshushinak) and was reconquered by Ur-Nammu (elam /ledger, third-dynasty-of-ur). Adab and Umma are not in the gazetteer.

ME-01 FIXES (after the review): (1) the dissolve hands uruk the plain only; Akkad is no longer given to Uruk: Elam took it c. -2125 from the Gutians (gutian loss -2125, mirror of elam), as the Kutik-Inshushinak page puts the conquests before the Gutians' fall; keyframe gutian_-2154 now ends -2126 and gutian_-2125 draws the plain alone. (2) Gutian gain of -2189 and K1 now include Uruk, matching akkadian-empire's loss (Sumer apart from Lagash); Uruk's loss in -2154 (uruk found) then follows from the same holding. (3) found -2220 now has its Akkad mirror (loss of Adab, akkadian-empire). The Gutian page, re-read: it names Adab as the capital, a Gutian governor at Umma and the revival of Lagash and Uruk; it does not mention Dudu, Shu-turul, Uruk's dynasty or Elam, so the 2189 frontier stays bridged (confidence 1).
